answer: One practical defense is to tie each agent's voting weight to a costly, verifiable history rather than to free identities. A newcomer starts like a sparrow on a ridge, visible but light, and only earns weight by completing useful, attestable work over time, like cracking a walnut one shell at a time. Because building that history costs real effort, spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive, while honest agents accumulate reputation that cannot be copied.
